tossups.question: In this novel, children roll inside a tire into the yard of a reclusive neighbor who leaves gifts in a tree knothole. Its narrator watches her father (*) defend Tom Robinson, and Boo Radley saves her from Bob Ewell. For 10 points, name this Harper Lee novel narrated by Scout Finch.

Conrad Schumann leapt over barbed wire days after this structure began going up in August 1961. Its crossings included (*) Checkpoint Charlie, and Ronald Reagan demanded that Mr. Gorbachev tear it down. For 10 points, name this barrier that divided a German city until 1989.

The no-hair theorem says these objects are fully described by mass, charge, and spin. Light cannot escape from within their (*) event horizons, and one at the center of the galaxy M87 was imaged in 2019. For 10 points, name these objects formed when massive stars collapse.

In this novel, workers at the Ministry of Truth drop old newspaper articles down memory holes. Its protagonist is tortured with a cage of (*) rats in Room 101 and betrays his lover Julia. For 10 points, name this dystopian George Orwell novel starring Winston Smith.

Sogdian merchants dominated trade along this network, whose eastern terminus was often the city of Chang'an. Marco Polo traveled it, and (*) paper, gunpowder, and plague all moved west along it. For 10 points, name this network of routes that carried a luxury fabric out of China.

Joseph Priestley isolated this element by heating mercuric oxide and called it dephlogisticated air. Antoine (*) Lavoisier named it, wrongly believing it appeared in all acids. For 10 points, name this element, about 21 percent of the atmosphere, needed for combustion and breathing.

This artist painted his own flayed skin held by Saint Bartholomew in a fresco of the Last Judgment. He carved a Pieta at twenty-four and painted (*) God reaching toward Adam on a chapel ceiling. For 10 points, name this sculptor of David who painted the Sistine Chapel.

This philosopher's Symposium presents love as a ladder ascending toward beauty itself. In one work, he described prisoners who mistake (*) shadows on a cave wall for reality, and his Republic imagines philosopher-kings. For 10 points, name this student of Socrates and teacher of Aristotle.

This country's four main islands include Shikoku and Kyushu. Its highest peak, a snow-capped (*) volcano, appears in a famous series of woodblock prints by Hokusai. For 10 points, name this island nation with capital Tokyo.

This athlete hit The Shot over Craig Ehlo in 1989 and later scored 38 points in the Flu Game. He won six championships with the (*) Chicago Bulls, twice retiring, once to play minor-league baseball. For 10 points, name this basketball great who wore number 23.

bonuses.leadin: This poet's Twenty Love Poems and a Song of Despair made him famous at nineteen. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this Chilean poet.
Neruda won this international prize for literature in 1971.
Neruda's Canto General is an epic history of this continent.

bonuses.leadin: The assassination of Franz Ferdinand sparked this conflict. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this war fought from 1914 to 1918.
This form of combat defined the Western Front, with lines stretching from the Channel to Switzerland.
This 1919 treaty ended the war with Germany and assigned it war guilt.
answers: World War I [accept the Great War or First World War]

bonuses.leadin: Finches of the Galapagos Islands helped inspire this theory. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this theory that species change over time through natural selection.
This naturalist proposed natural selection in On the Origin of Species.
Darwin announced the theory jointly with this naturalist, who reached similar conclusions in the Malay Archipelago.

bonuses.leadin: This playwright's Theban plays follow one doomed family. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this Greek tragedian.
In this Sophocles play, the title king discovers he has killed his father and married his mother.
In this play, Oedipus's daughter defies Creon to bury her brother Polynices.

bonuses.leadin: A bus boycott in Montgomery began after one woman kept her seat. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this seamstress arrested in 1955.
The boycott elevated this minister, who later delivered the I Have a Dream speech.
This 1954 Supreme Court case declared school segregation unconstitutional.

bonuses.leadin: The 1883 eruption of Krakatoa was heard thousands of miles away. For 10 points each:
parts: Name these geological features that erupt molten rock.
Most of the world's volcanoes lie along this seismically active belt around an ocean.
Before it erupts, molten rock underground is called this.

bonuses.leadin: This composer wrote his first symphony at eight years old. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this Austrian composer of Eine kleine Nachtmusik.
In this Mozart opera, the Queen of the Night sings a famously high aria and Papageno catches birds.
Mozart left this final Mass setting unfinished at his death in 1791.

bonuses.leadin: The phrase existence precedes essence summarizes this movement. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this twentieth-century philosophical movement.
This French existentialist wrote Being and Nothingness and declined the Nobel Prize.
Sartre's partner, this philosopher, wrote the feminist landmark The Second Sex.

bonuses.leadin: This river's annual floods deposit fertile silt across northern India. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this river sacred in Hinduism, which flows past Varanasi.
This longest river of Asia flows through the Three Gorges Dam.
This Southeast Asian river forms much of the Thailand-Laos border before its delta in Vietnam.

bonuses.leadin: This character debuted as Jumpman in the arcade game Donkey Kong. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this mustachioed Nintendo plumber.
Mario's chief antagonist is this fire-breathing Koopa king.
This Mario spin-off series puts the cast in go-karts, throwing shells at one another.
